scope: E0 over odd-degree binary fields; ECC2K-130 uses degree131

cards.title: Existentially eliminate full-point witnesses on a certified finite domain
cards.mechanism: Validate every supplied base point in T_n, retain exactly its allowed x codes, omit redundant ordinate membership witnesses, and lift/replay actual supplied points.
cards.evidence: models.json circuits; seven native checks, including sign-restricted bases and n83/131 singleton controls
cards.next_action: Run explicit/certified encodings on the same non-singleton bases, unseen known-answer targets, all identity patterns, seeds and cumulative budgets; account for base admission and successful original-group replay.
cards.discriminates: Lower complete successful work supports this encoding specialization; larger search or more UNKNOWN outcomes despite fewer variables rejects the assumed propagation benefit on those workloads.
cards.limitations: Only finite validated domains; no generic algebraic subspace certificate, asymptotic improvement or measured timing. Existing explicit mode remains default.

cards.title: Restrict the second trace bit before ordinate elimination
cards.mechanism: Compute q|V and its polar rank on the existing trace-zero x subspace. If q|V is linear, eliminate y0 without cubic terms. The retained ECC2K-130 d16 polynomial window has q|V=0.
cards.evidence: models.json subspaces; exact n3/5/7 restricted point checks and actual n83/131 profiles
cards.next_action: Compare actual restricted raw/compact/factored relation systems on a fixed base and target set; measure solving degree and successful work, not just single-point counts.
cards.discriminates: A lower matched solving degree or successful-work cost supports the representation. A degree/cost increase despite q simplification limits its utility without invalidating the point-model identity.
cards.limitations: Does not change allowed points, relation yield or kernel cardinality. General restricted q need not be linear; n83,d64 is a retained counter-control.

cards.title: Complete quadratic full-point relation chains on linear-q windows
cards.mechanism: Use the quadratic restricted full-point model and lifted slope/point-addition equations instead of eliminating y into a cubic S3 chain. Include generic addition, doubling, opposite points and identity branches completely.
cards.evidence: TZL-02 supplies the quadratic summand models only; no complete relation encoding or performance result yet
cards.next_action: Construct a branch-complete Boolean relation builder with explicit nonzero guards and all identity cases; exhaustively compare with group enumeration at n5/7 before matched solver checks.
cards.discriminates: Exact lifts plus lower measured solving degree may offset extra variables. Any missing branch or false refutation rejects the construction; more total successful work rejects the proposed tradeoff on tested instances.
cards.limitations: More point/slope variables than unlifted x-only S3; S3 itself also has a quadratic lifting and the native AND/XOR circuit already uses it. Compare that baseline too. Quadratic input degree does not imply quadratic solving degree. No arbitrary-algebra geometric chart is claimed.

cards.title: Rank-aware presentation choice at fixed factor base
cards.mechanism: Use actual q polar rank, product-span dimension and term/auxiliary counts to choose among raw, compact and factored presentations without changing V or the base.
cards.evidence: n131,d16 compact remains quadratic; n83,d64 compact is cubic with10646 AND auxiliaries versus7328 in raw/factored
cards.next_action: Freeze a train/held-out protocol over fixed subspaces and targets, compare the selector with every fixed presentation and a charged portfolio. Count construction, rejected attempts and replay.
cards.discriminates: Held-out successful-work savings support a selector; rank-only prediction failures or selection overhead exceeding gains reject that selector, not every encoding.
cards.limitations: Profile is not a solver-cost theorem. Subspace search and basis changes are different experiments requiring matched-size/null controls.
